question.text: An exporter hedges EUR 500,000 receivable by buying 500 lots of EURINR put at strike 91.00, premium Rs. 0.30. At expiry, EURINR is 92.50. What is the effective realization?

explanation.text: The Logic: Put is OTM (spot 92.50 > strike 91.00), so it is not exercised. Exporter sells at spot 92.50 and bears only the premium paid: 92.50 - 0.30 = Rs. 92.20 per EUR. The protective put preserves upside participation when the exchange rate rises. The Trap: Rs. 91.00 assumes the put is exercised (not optimal when spot > strike). Rs. 90.70 is Strike - Premium, which applies only if the put is exercised. Note: Protective put mechanics: if spot rises above strike, the put is abandoned and net realization equals spot minus premium.
